purpose: Document ORT Web WASM rung blocker for INT4 export
finding: INT4 export uses external data files (encoder.onnx.data, decoder.onnx.data, joint.onnx.data) totaling ~755 MB. ORT Web WASM in Node fails with: 'Failed to load external data file encoder.onnx.data, error: Module.MountedFiles is not available.' This is because ORT Web uses an Emscripten-emulated filesystem (Module.MountedFiles) that doesn't work in Node.js by default for external data files.

results.plain_path: FAILS on external data load: Module.MountedFiles unavailable
results.backslash_path: FAILS on external data load: Module.MountedFiles unavailable
results.file_url: FAILS with ENOENT: path treated as relative (cwd-joined)

workaround_options: Convert INT4 to single-file ONNX (no external data) — would require re-export from PyTorch with use_external_data_format=False
Use onnxruntime-node (native binding, not WASM) — bypasses the Emscripten limitation but isn't the WASM rung
Use onnxruntime-web in a browser environment where Module.MountedFiles works natively
Pre-load external data into memory and pass as Tensor inputs instead of file paths
next_session: Pick a workaround. The most practical: try onnxruntime-web in a headless browser environment (Playwright/puppeteer) to verify the WASM rung in-browser. The Node WASM approach is blocked by infrastructure, not by model parity.
